title: A second `IHDR`
why:
**Permitted is not the same as well-placed.** Every chunk here is on the allowlist and the file is still malformed — a conforming decoder rejects it, so admitting it on membership alone reaches a gate verdict where the other side reaches `decode-failed`. There are only five chunks to constrain, which is what the allowlist bought: the structural rules are finite because the vocabulary is.

The second `IHDR` sits before the image data, so the preflight reaches it first and refuses it as `header-invalid` — a repeat of a chunk that may appear once, at a position where the prefix walk admits only `PLTE` and `tRNS`. `decode-failed-trns-after-idat` is the same placement rule on the far side of `IDAT`, where the decoder is the one that catches it.
